owen_marketing: Heads up 2 5 We need a tight benchmark packet for the launch demo + webinar. Ask: reproducible artifacts + short summary lines for each claim. Focus areas: streaming gen tail (token flush latency), embeddings for search demo (batch=16), and end-to-end cost/1k tokens. Can runtime run a focused smoke today and a full sweep during the Tue overnight window?

sam_runtime: We can. Two clarifying q's: which exact tags, do you want streaming (flush interval) knobs varied, and what's the target sample size for the streaming microcohort? Also where to put embargoed artifacts?

owen_marketing: Models: redwood-alpha-7b:fp16 (v2026-03-01) and redwood-alpha-7b:quant6 (v2026-03-07). Streaming: test flush intervals 20ms and 50ms; microcohort = 3k 1-turn interactive prompts (~150 tokens avg) for streaming; embeds = 4k items batch=16. Smoke = 40 samples per variant/flush; full sweep = streaming 3k, long-complete 1k, embeds 4k. Use payload s3://redwood-internal/marketing/payloads/launch-webinar-stream-v1.json. Drop to s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-2109876543/ with embargo ACL.

zack_ops: I'll create the s3 folder and set embargo to 2026-04-05; watchers: marketing + platform-metrics.

sam_runtime: Measurement defs for clarity: 
- "streaming token flush latency": time from model emit event to byte available to client (server-side).
- "end-to-end gen latency": request receive -> last token sent.
- "cold-start": first request after >5m idle.
We will produce per-request CSV (request_id, model, variant, flush_ms, seq_in, seq_out, tokens, latency_ms, gpu_pct, trace_link) and 50 annotated traces. We'll use seed=20260401 for reproducibility.

daria_comms: Legal prefers fixed tolerances in the request so we can pre-clear phrasing. Suggested public tolerances: p95 within headline +/-8% and cost delta <=12%. For streaming statements, prefer absolute ms numbers for cold-start.

sam_runtime: Acknowledged. Plan: run smoke today (40 samples) with both flush settings. If smoke within tolerances we schedule full sweep Tue 02:00-06:00. If you want faster completion we can reserve burst capacity (ops approval required). Perf CLI snippet we'll include in artifacts.

perf-bot: queued bench-2109876543-smoke (est 1h).

perf-bot: bench-2109876543-smoke completed  summary at s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-2109876543/smoke/summary.csv. Preliminary highlights: fp16 streaming p95 (flush20ms) = 160ms, fp16 streaming p95 (flush50ms) = 145ms, quant6 streaming p95 (flush20ms) = 177ms (+10% vs fp16 flush20), embeds (batch16 p95) = 24ms, estimated cost delta quant6 ~11% lower. Raw traces uploaded.

owen_marketing: Great  can you draft one-line summaries and an embargo blurb? Also include the perf CLI command and a recommended short phrasing for the product page.

sam_runtime: Draft one-liners (prelim): 
- redwood-alpha-7b:fp16  streaming p95 (flush20ms) 160ms steady-state; baseline cost.
- redwood-alpha-7b:quant6  streaming p95 (flush20ms) 177ms (+10%), cost ~11% lower on test payload.
- Embeddings (batch=16): p95 24ms.
Embargoed blurb (internal): "Internal benchmarks on representative streaming and embedding workloads show quantized variants reduce per-token compute cost with measured tail latency tradeoffs; see appendix for methodology, flush settings, and raw traces."

daria_comms: Tweak: replace "measured" with "measured" (tone check) and add methodology link s3://redwood-internal/marketing/bench-2109876543/methodology.txt. Also recommend we avoid the word "identical" for quantized parity claims.

sam_runtime: Got it. We'll include exact perf command and a short ops note on the run. Full sweep queued pending ops burst approval; we'll post job id bench-2109876543-full when started.
